headline: Vaniq-Edge: 34MB local TTS engine boasts 2.94% Word Error Rate
summary: This ~8.5M parameter standalone engine delivers 24kHz mono audio with minimal latency, aiming to solve the trade-off between model size and speech quality for local conversational agents.
details: Building local conversational voice agents often means choosing between large, slow models and tiny ones with poor speech quality. Vaniq-Edge aims to bridge this gap, offering a compact solution without sacrificing clarity.
Vaniq-Edge is an end-to-end, ~8.5M parameter standalone local TTS engine. It processes text into 24kHz mono audio without requiring external vocoders or second-stage models.
The primary goal of Vaniq-Edge is to maintain a low Word Error Rate (WER), achieving 2.94%. This ensures the output remains clear and understandable, even with long or complex sentences.
The developer encourages users to test the engine with challenging text, such as unusual names, numbers, or tongue twisters, to evaluate its performance on edge cases.

headline_marked: [[Astronomers detect first exomoon]] orbiting a brown dwarf 73 light-years away
headline: Astronomers detect first exomoon orbiting a brown dwarf 73 light-years away
summary: An international team has found evidence of a moon-like body, at least 0.9 times Jupiter's mass, challenging conventional definitions of celestial objects.
details: An international research team has discovered evidence of a moonlike body, marking the first time such an object has been detected outside our solar system. This object orbits the brown dwarf CD-35 2722 B, located 73 light-years away, and has a mass of at least 0.9 times that of Jupiter.

Brown dwarfs are celestial bodies between planets and stars, lacking the mass to become a star. The team observed CD-35 2722 B using the CRIRES+ infrared spectrograph on the European Southern Observatory’s Very Large Telescope (VLT) over 23 nights.

They employed the Doppler method to capture how the brown dwarf wobbles, indicating the gravitational pull of an orbiting body. This technique, previously used for exoplanet discoveries, enabled measurements up to 100 times more precise than previous attempts.

Published in Nature, the analysis revealed a strong signal for a large moon orbiting over approximately 170 days. Its mass ratio to the brown dwarf is about 2.5%, significantly higher than any moon-to-planet ratio in our solar system.

The object's unique position blurs the lines between stars, planets, and moons, making its classification complex. Researchers are still grappling with whether it should be officially called a moon, as there is no universally recognized definition for such objects.
